Welcome, Yankees brother. 

Many of us will regard the late 90’s as the golden era from our lifetime. I would learn all the Yankees history you can but many alive now all have this era in common and consider the “Core Four” to be the benchmark we use to measure a Yankee player’s greatness. 

Last season we were very excited about Gleyber Torres and Miguel Andujar. Towards the end of the season we quickly became enamored with Luke Voit. Many here are gay for him—not in a sexual way, just if you were trapped in a log cabin and...never mind. Do not be alarmed by seeing the amount of discussion dedicated to comparing the sizes of the Yankees’ “dongs”. We love Yankee dongs. Especially the big swinging ones. 

Despite the rare “golden sombrero”, Aaron Judge is Our Lord and Savior, he who will shepherd us through the darkness. Gary Sanchez is a phenomenal player, when he can manage to get out of his own way. Suffice it to say he is exciting to watch and will almost always spike your heart rate for good or bad.

Our starting pitching isn’t regarded as the best in baseball but we are lucky to have Masahiro Tanaka and you are fortunate to see CC Sabathia pitch in his final season. CC is one of the longest serving Yankees along with Brett Gardner whose future with the Yankees is questionable. Injuries have plagued the team early on and so Gardner gets to start with Aaron Hicks and Giancarlo Stanton (the giant) both out. Oh, and another outfielder who is also injured, Jacoby Elsbury. Let us know if you spot him. He’s gone missing without a sighting for a long time now.

The bullpen (a name you’ll hear for all of the relief pitchers given where they sit) was regarded as one of the best in all of baseball but we are waiting for them to get into the groove. Adam Ottavino, a relief pitcher, has some pretty great movement on his pitches and an even better Instagram account.

The competition for a starting job is higher this season than I can remember for a while. As I said, with players injured, some guys who would most likely be on the Minor League team (Triple A; AAA) have been called up and given a chance to contribute. Some have done more with this opportunity than others—worth mentioning Clint Frazier here. In addition to filling in for injured players, we had some competition at First Base for the starting job between Luke Voit and Greg Bird (the guy who actually looks like a bird) but again with injuries, management has had some room to maneuver and has taken advantage or utilized the Designated Hitter slot. The designated hitter (DH) is unique to the American League. In the National League you’ll see pitchers most likely batting ninth in the lineup but in the AL the pitcher is protected from having to hit.

Speaking of managers, we have had a line of succession starting from the era i mention earlier with Joe Torre, then Joe Girardi and now Aaron Boone. I’d say Boone has yet to win the hearts of the Yankee fan base as a manager (see Boone as a player Game 7) since he took the job from Girardi who was fired reportedly for his differences in approach with Brian Cashman (CashGod) who along with Hal Steinbrenner manages the Front Office or business side of things. It is believed that Cashman is heavily influenced by his team of analytics specialists who are sciencing the game and using statistics and complex mathematics to determine how they should make decisions. Some say Boone was picked because he would get out of the way and allow this to happen. When things aren’t going well it is common to hear people blaming the manager and occasionally calling for their firing. Don’t confuse this frustration with the actual hatred we have for other teams, specifically the Boston Red Sox. 

Also, above all else, remember this truth...

DAVID ORTIZ DID STEROIDS
